---
title: "Experiment Design"
---

::: {.callout-warning}
This is a working draft. Key decisions marked **[TO RESOLVE]** depend on
literature review findings and consultation with the device inventor.
:::

## Purpose

A preliminary feasibility study to determine whether training with the balance
device produces measurable changes in golf swing weight
transfer patterns sufficient to justify a formal trial.

This is not a clinical trial. It is preliminary data collection by a golf
instructor with participants drawn from their teaching practice.

---

## Research Question

> Does a [X]-week training programme using the balance device produce
> measurable changes in centre of pressure timing or magnitude during the
> golf swing in amateur golfers?

Secondary: Are any changes in COP pattern associated with changes in ball
direction consistency?

---

## Design

**Type**: Pre-post observational study (no control group at this stage)
**Rationale**: Control group requires larger n and matched participants.
Pre-post is appropriate for feasibility work where the primary question is
"does anything change" before testing "is the device the cause."

**[TO RESOLVE]**: Whether a small waitlist control group (n=3-4) is achievable
within the instructor's teaching pool.

---

## Participants

**Target n**: 8-12 golfers
**Rationale**: Large enough to detect a meaningful group trend; small enough
to be feasible for one instructor. Literature suggests n=10-15 for pilot
proprioceptive intervention studies.

**Inclusion criteria**:
- Established golfer (plays regularly, not a beginner)
- Right-handed **[TO RESOLVE: include left-handed separately?]**
- No current lower limb injury
- Able to commit to training period

**Exclusion criteria**:
- Current lower limb injury or surgery within 12 months
- Neurological conditions affecting balance
- Unable to wear the device safely

**Recruitment**: Instructor's existing pupils — opportunistic sample,
acknowledged limitation.

---

## Intervention

**Device**: Balance device, one pair
**Training period**: **[TO RESOLVE — 4 or 6 weeks?]** — literature suggests
4-6 weeks for proprioceptive adaptations to appear
**Frequency**: **[TO RESOLVE]** — suggest minimum 3 sessions/week
**Duration per session**: 15-20 minutes device use
**Activity during device use**: Slow practice swings without ball initially,
progressing to full swings with ball

**Standardisation needed**:
- Consistent camera position at all sessions (mark floor position)
- Same club used for all measurement sessions (7-iron suggested —
  standard in literature)
- Warm-up protocol standardised

---

## Measurement Points

- **T0**: Baseline — before any device use
- **T1**: Mid-point — after 2-3 weeks **[TO RESOLVE]**
- **T2**: Post-intervention — immediately after training period ends
- **T3**: Retention — 2-4 weeks after device use stops **[OPTIONAL — adds
  significant burden]**

---

## Outcome Measures

See [Outcome Measures](measures.qmd) for full rationale.

**Primary**:
- Centre of pressure timing (when does COP shift from trail to lead foot)
- COP magnitude at key swing events

**Secondary**:
- Ball direction consistency (if launch monitor available)
- Subjective feel rating (simple 1-10 scale per session)

**Measurement tools**:
**[TO RESOLVE]** — depends on what is accessible:

| Option | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|
| Pressure insoles (Moticon/Pedar rental) | Direct COP measurement | Cost, calibration |
| Force plate (if Loughborough involved) | Gold standard | Requires lab visit |
| Video face-on + manual coding | Free, feasible now | Indirect, labour intensive |
| Phone IMU | Free, portable | Accuracy unknown for this use |

**Minimum viable option**: Face-on video with manual frame-by-frame coding of
weight transfer timing. Not ideal but generates preliminary data.

---

## Ethics Considerations

This is instructor-led data collection on willing pupils, not a formal clinical
trial. However:

- Participants should give informed consent to data collection and potential
  publication of anonymised findings
- Data should be stored securely (not just on personal devices)
- Any adverse events (falls, discomfort) should be recorded
- If approaching Loughborough, ethics approval will be required before they
  can formally participate

**[TO RESOLVE]**: Draft a simple participant information sheet and consent form
before data collection begins.

---

## Limitations (pre-acknowledged)

- No control group — cannot attribute change to device vs natural improvement
  or regression to mean
- Small n — insufficient power for definitive conclusions
- Opportunistic sample — instructor's pupils, not representative
- Measurement tools may be indirect — video coding not equivalent to force plate
- Single instructor — cannot separate device effect from coaching effect
- No blinding possible — participants know they are using the device
